title: Throwing a flared serving bowl in stoneware
subtitle: A wide, outward-flaring bowl with a simple foot ring in smooth stoneware
excerpt: A flared serving bowl has walls that open outward from a narrow base to a wide mouth, creating a low, generous form suitable for salads, fruit, or display. The flare is achieved by pulling the wall outward more than upward. This tutorial covers a 32 cm wide bowl from 900 g of smooth stoneware.
sourceNotes: Technique synthesised from standard wheel-throwing references and practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: An outward opening of the pot wall, where the rim is wider than the body below it
The drying stage where clay holds its shape and can be trimmed without collapsing

content.text: achieved by pulling the wall outward at a shallow angle on each pull rather than pulling upward. Large flared bowls are thrown on a bat because the soft form cannot be safely moved from the wheel head. At 900 g, the bat is essential.
Fix a bat to the wheel head. Centre 900 g into a wide, low mound. Open the centre with a palm and three fingers to a floor 8 mm thick, spreading outward to a base diameter of about 12 cm.
Compress the floor with the wooden rib, working from centre outward in two passes at medium wheel speed.

On the first pull, angle the outer hand so the wall opens outward at roughly 45 degrees rather than vertical. Use the inner hand to support and push the clay outward as the outer hand guides from outside.

On each subsequent pull, increase the outward angle slightly. The goal is a wall that rises from the base at an angle of about 30 degrees from horizontal at the rim, giving the wide shallow bowl shape.
Keep the rim rolling inward slightly at the end of each pull to prevent the wall thinning too fast at the top edge. The wall should be 6 to 8 mm thick at all points.
Hold the metal rib against the outside of the wall to compress and smooth it. Needle-trim the rim level. Aim for a finished rim diameter of 30 to 32 cm and a height of about 8 cm at the centre.
, invert on the wheel and trim a foot ring about 14 mm in diameter at the base. The foot ring lifts the base clear and gives the wide bowl a refined, finished look underneath.

items.problem: Rim collapses outward and the bowl spreads too flat
items.cause: The wall was pulled outward too aggressively with insufficient thickness at the rim to hold its shape
items.fix: Re-centre the clay if still soft and reform the rim by supporting the outside and pushing slightly inward to restore the curve. Next time, keep the rim rolling inward at the end of each pull to maintain thickness and control at the edge

items.problem: Floor cracks in a ring 5 to 8 cm from the centre after drying
items.cause: Insufficient compression of the floor during throwing left the clay thin and stressed
items.fix: Apply two compression passes with a wooden rib at medium wheel speed after opening. On a large bowl, an outer compression pass after the final pull also helps consolidate the floor where the wall joins it
